opportunities.title: Grinch and Kisses holiday packs -> on-pack conversion funnel
opportunities.what_is_happening: Hershey's 2026 holiday line includes co-branded Dr. Seuss Grinch packaging, including a giftable Grinch milk chocolate bar 6-pack. Hershey's Kisses is also launching a limited-edition holiday gift-wrapping foil kit based on its Kisses foil packaging.
opportunities.why_flowcode: Licensed and limited-edition holiday packs reach national shoppers, but the Grinch pack shows no measurable digital next step and no first-party capture. Flowcodes on pack leading to a FlowHub (sweepstakes, gifting ideas), with every scanner captured in FlowID, would turn seasonal packs into a CRM conversion funnel. Because the destination can change after printing, the same codes can carry later campaigns.
opportunities.confidence_why: Two signals from Hershey's own press release agree on the holiday packaging lineup.
opportunities.size_why: Packaging on a national brand's holiday line.
opportunities.timing_why: Holiday line announced Nov 5 and in market for the current season.
opportunities.suggested_play: Capri Sun put a scannable code on the front of a licensed pack that led to a sweepstakes and drove 28K+ sweepstakes submissions, making it a Top 3 performing code across the Kraft Heinz portfolio. Hershey could run the same model on Grinch and Kisses holiday packs: a Flowcode opens a holiday FlowHub, and each scanner is captured in FlowID and synced to the CRM. The code's destination can then rotate to Valentine's or Easter without reprinting. The Kisses kit signal shows QR codes or links are already in use, so the pitch is to upgrade those to measured, identity-linked connections.
opportunities.first_step: Ask the Hershey's holiday Brand Manager whether the Kisses kit links feed the CRM today. Share the Capri Sun case study as a template for the next seasonal print run.

opportunities.title: Reese's Trick-or-Treatiest Street -> attributed social and creator links
opportunities.what_is_happening: Reese's ran a Halloween campaign to find the Trick-or-Treatiest Street in America using data, community insights and a first-ever Halloween Council. The council, including creators and celebrities Christina Ricci and Kathy Najimy, documented 150 streets in a two-part social content series.
opportunities.why_flowcode: The social series shows link usage, but creator and social traffic is not tied to a persistent identity or to Reese's offline touchpoints. FlowURLs in creator posts, leading to a shared FlowHub and FlowID, would attribute each creator's connections and capture entrants as first-party contacts.
opportunities.confidence_why: The brand's own newsroom release and trade press agree.
opportunities.size_why: A multi-market national social and creator campaign.
opportunities.timing_why: Halloween has passed; the campaign is likely to recur seasonally, though that is not confirmed.
opportunities.suggested_play: GoBowling ran QR codes and short URLs across events, TV coverage and social, with 821 completed entries recorded via FlowID at an 86% form conversion rate. For next Halloween, Reese's could give each Halloween Council creator a unique FlowURL, with street nominations flowing into one FlowHub and FlowID. That would show which creator drove entries and build a first-party audience.
opportunities.first_step: Request a Halloween recap call with the Reese's Social / Digital Marketing lead. Ask how creator-driven traffic was attributed, then propose FlowURLs for the 2027 planning cycle.
